newsitem.title: USA: Latam in forefront of U.S. foreign crude trade.
newsitem.headline: Latam in forefront of U.S. foreign crude trade.

text.p: Latin American activity stood at the forefront of U.S. foreign crude activity, traders said on Friday.
In what appeared to be the first October sale, a trading house on Thursday sold an Ecuadoran Oriente cargo to a U.S. East Coast refiner for October 5-10 delivery.
The cargo was sold at an equivalent to around November West Texas Intermediate/Cushing minus $3.05 a barrel, traders said.
Meanwhile, sellers of Colombian Cusiana crude have toughened their positions, and were heard offering around 75 cents under October WTI for end-September cargoes.
Potential buyers, however, reacted skeptically. "The appetite has gone away," one regular buyer said, referring to a flurry of Cusiana sales earlier in the week at around $1.05 to $1.10
Two cargoes were still available for late September loading, traders said.
Market talk of possible Cusiana loading delays in September due to production hiccups could not be immediately confirmed.
Separately, Uruguay's state oil refiner ANCAP is seeking to buy one million barrels of crude oil for October 1-10 arrival, a trade source said.
Bids are due August 20, with an award due on August 21.

The tender was initially supposed to be issued on August 8, but the company postponed it to accommodate a scheduled maintenance of the topping unit of the 34,600 barrels per day (bpd) La Teja refinery.
The unit was shut down on August 10 and is expected to resume operations around August 20.
ANCAP is seeking crude with an American Petroleum Institute (API) gravity range of 26-45 degrees and a sulfur content of 0.5 percent to 1.8 percent.
Eslewhere in the region, Peruvian state oil company Petroperu issued a tender to buy 380,000 barrels of crude oil for October 8-10 arrival, trade sources said.
Offers are due August 19, with a decision slated for August 20.

Possible candidates listed are Colombia's Caqo Limsn, South Blend, Vasconia and Cusiana grades, Venezuela's Mesa, Lagotreco and Guafita, Ecuador's Oriente, Peru's Lote 8, Mexico's Isthmus, and Argentina's Medanito, Rincon and Escalante.
Petroperu recently bought Lote 8 crude in another crude tender issued in early August for August 29-31 arrival at the Talara refinery.
The company infrequently issues such tenders since the privatization of the La Pampilla refinery last year.
